method: Model visual inspection of extracted frames through view_image; not human real-time viewing and not continuous video playback.
conclusion: No blocking geometry pop, wrong early assembly direction, annotation target error or hidden shoulder was observed within the sampled range. One minor branding-background overlap remains. These samples cannot certify every intervening frame or real-time motion pacing.

checks.result: No sudden model disappearance in the sampled consecutive triplets. Exploded members retain coherent relative positions; wide-to-detail travel preserves scene identity.
The tenon marker points to the protruding end; mortise marker sits on the lower aperture lip; the shoulder remains visible through the translucent adjacent column in frames1049 onward.
The brace is labeled on the actual inclined member. In the sampled assembly sequence the prepared beam-brace unit remains coherent while columns close horizontally.

The peg advances toward its aligned opening rather than visibly entering a solid column face; removal is shown before the columns separate. Full-resolution frame1680 confirms marker-to-peg attachment.
The group bracket encloses the front bent; the longitudinal label targets a genuine longitudinal beam. Its final horizontal travel is the designed label exit, rather than a physical anchor jump.
The translucent column in frame2432 reveals distinct joint elevations and does not require a fake duplicate model.
The exploded bracket groups stay consistent during camera approach through frame3027; the group marker encloses multiple real components.
